biggest_gap.what: Every screen draws its panel at the same fixed rect [200, 160, 1520, 780] — 57.2% of a 1920x1080 frame — whatever it is holding, because game/src/ui/chrome.js:70 defines ONE constant BOX consumed by screenRect() and therefore by every screen through screen(). RI-UIX09 P4 requires D2 >= 0.35 of that rect to be matter and hard-fails below 0.15. Measured on captures I took at 7c63111d and sanity-checked with tools/visual/frame-liveness.mjs (8 frames, all LIVE): journal 0.1314, level-up 0.0910, sheet 0.0895, spells 0.0702, container 0.0572 — FIVE HARD FAILS — and inventory 0.1524, the only populated screen above the floor and still less than half the bar. Two independent implementations of the item's own method 4 agree to four decimals on all six screens. The arithmetic that matters is the good news inside it, re-derived here rather than quoted from S56: at the matter each screen ALREADY draws, D2 >= 0.35 is reached at 24.9% of frame for the inventory, 21.5% for the journal, 14.9% for level-up, 14.6% for the sheet, 11.5% for spells and 9.3% for the container. Morrowind's own inventory window is about 24% of its frame. This is a sizing defect, not a content defect, and round 3 reported it undone rather than half-done — it did not pad a number and it did not add decorative fill.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player opens the character sheet, the spell list, the level-up room or the journal and finds a room three-fifths furnished and two-fifths empty — six screens in a row that look unfinished, which is the first impression the interface makes and the one the owner will get in the first minute.

remedy.action: Replace game/src/ui/chrome.js:70's single `BOX = { x: 200, y: 160, w: 1520, h: 780 }` with a per-screen rect looked up by mode and consumed by screenRect(), then re-pitch each screen's absolute sc.inner offsets against its own box. TAKE THE FOUR CHEAP ONES FIRST — the journal (screens/text.js), the level-up screen and the character sheet (screens/progress.js) and the spell list all position against sc.inner in offsets that shrink cleanly, and the sheet additionally needs its skills column re-derived because it is written to FILL ih, which makes its contents height circular. LEAVE THE INVENTORY FOR A SECOND STEP: screens/inventory.js's COLS needs 200+20+132+24+640+30 = 1046 units of width before the detail panel gets any, so it cannot reach 24.9% by shrinking alone and needs its columns re-pitched, and it puts the worn band at iy + 476*s, the sort control at iy + 574*s and gold at iy + ih - 40*s, so any height below about 614 units collides.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-UIX03 P7 states the equip commitment UNCONDITIONALLY — 'changing an equipped weapon or armour piece costs an animation-committed action of >= 30 frames during which the player is vulnerable' — while its own Comparison method step 5 measures it CONDITIONALLY: 'Equip a different weapon from the menu DURING COMBAT; assert the trace shows a committed state of >= 30 frames with iframe: false'. M-P5 is scored on that run and only that run. Round 3 set the commitment to 0 frames out of combat and left it at 30 in a fight. Does M-P5's hard fail ('instant equip swap') fire on the out-of-combat case?
arbitration_questions.side_a: It does not. Out of combat the world is stopped — M-P1 measures frame delta 0 of 120 — so the window in which 'the player is vulnerable' can be true has measure zero, and a cost taken out of a stopped clock is a hang rather than a cost. CLAUDE.md's settling rule points here: Souls wins INSIDE the fight; Morrowind wins everywhere else. RI-UIX10's own bar cites Morrowind's inventory by name: 'the moment you equip something the figure in the corner is wearing it.' The item's comparison method scopes the measurement to a fight in the only place it is measured.
arbitration_questions.side_b: It does. P7's property text carries no qualifier and a build may not amend a property by implementing around it. RI-UIX10 O3 — the row that failed this last round — explicitly does NOT require the commitment to be short: it allows 30 frames provided the screen says so, and round 3 ALSO built the saying-so (IC1: 'Putting on the bog-iron maul. You are standing still for it.'). So O3 could have been satisfied without touching the commitment at all, which means the change was not forced by the gap it answers.
arbitration_questions.scored_as: M-P5 pass, on the item's own comparison method. If side B is adopted, M-P5 hard-fails and RI-UIX03 drops from 3 to 2; the piece score does not move either way.
arbitration_questions.for_owner: RI-UIX03's dimension owner, by append to the item — either qualify P7's property text with 'in combat', or state the out-of-combat commitment AND name what the player is vulnerable to on a stopped clock.

self_audit.self_audit_note: THREE FALSE, AND ONE FLAG, ALL STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. (1) `ran_every_assigned_method` is FALSE: three played gates (RI-UIX06 §G, RI-UIX07 §G/V11, RI-UIX08 §G) need fresh agents and CLAUDE.md rule 0 forbids me spawning them — rule 0e places that with the orchestrator; RI-UIX01 §D is unmeasured for the third round and I recommend it become its own piece; RI-UIX03 C4 was not run for the third round; RI-UIX06's FIDELITY sweep was not run and AD4 was not re-run on the admissible stimulus; RI-UIX07 E-T5's deletion arm and V10's pixel half were not run; W6 (breath) was never made true; and RI-UIX03 §B-§E were carried rather than re-run behind an empty `git diff -- game/data/`. Every one is in method_deviations or in its check's note, and every one is scored fail-closed rather than omitted. (2) `blind_done_where_required` is FALSE: three items carry a blind pair or a §G gate and none could be run, for the same reason each time. (3) `saw_builder_notes_before_blind` is TRUE in the critic block: my dispatch brief handed me the round-2 verdict and the builder's status file up front, which departs from §8's ordering. I mitigated it the only way still available — the two instruments that carry the most weight in this verdict are the ROUND-2 CRITIC'S OWN, run byte-identical, so their pass conditions were fixed before either document existed; my own probe measures things neither document measures (O3 at fifteen frames instead of sixty, the journal exit by every advertised route, both sub-views, the repeat on both device arms); and the two claims I make AGAINST the builder's own account are that three of drive.mjs's reds are instrument defects the builder did not identify, and that its in-combat narration IS legible enough to declare and photograph, which it fail-closed on itself. The verdict is PROVISIONAL on that flag by §8's own rule and I record it rather than let it pass silently. `escalation_ladder_used_if_gap_seemed_small` is TRUE and it is what produced this round's real findings: I zoomed in (fifteen frames instead of sixty, f+1 instead of f+15), changed the sample (the ugly one — the refused item, the misc item, the OTHER sub-view, the second door into the reset), stressed it (a query with letters in it rather than an empty one, three flicks rather than one, both device arms of the same hold), compared the second-order property (not 'is there an exit' but 'does the exit do what the screen PROMISES'), and asked what a player notices in the first minute — which is the question the density table answers and the reason this piece still fails.

notes: ORDERING, per §8: I read the round-2 verdict and the builder's status file at the start because my dispatch brief contained them, and I record that as saw_builder_notes_before_blind: true. I read the gap ledger for ui.menu.journal only AFTER my raw measurements were taken, to check closure. CONFLICT OF INTEREST: none. I built none of this, I am not the round-1 or round-2 critic, and I did not write RI-UIX09 or RI-UIX10 — which matters this round, because RI-UIX10 is the item that moves from 2 to 8 and the agent scoring it is not the agent who wrote it. §1.3 SUFFICIENCY, RECORDED EVEN THOUGH I CONCLUDE THE BAR IS FINE: I checked whether these items can express what this piece needs to be good at, and they can. The one candidate hole is the axis repeat — a list you can walk one press at a time is 'operable' under RI-UIX10 O1 and no item asks whether walking it is bearable. I checked the whole relevant corpus before deciding, and these are the ids: RI-UIX01, RI-UIX02, RI-UIX03, RI-UIX04, RI-UIX05, RI-UIX06, RI-UIX07, RI-UIX08, RI-UIX09, RI-UIX10, RI-JRN02, RI-JRN03, RI-JRN04, RI-JRN09, RI-CAM02. I did NOT extend the bar, for two reasons: RI-JRN03 KB2 already legislates key auto-repeat in the OPPOSITE direction ('every handler checks event.repeat and ignores repeats'), so a new row demanding repeat would collide with an existing one rather than fill a hole, and §1.3 lets me only add and never weaken; and it is not what caps this piece — the cap is RI-UIX09 DN4, which the corpus expresses precisely. Two of the seven items I was handed were written by the two previous critics under this same rule, and a third would have been a reflex rather than a finding. ONE CORPUS BUG IS FILED IN why_not_ten RATHER THAN ABSORBED INTO A SCORE: RI-UIX10's ladder tops out at 8 and has no 9 or 10 rung, so as written it cannot express 'beats the reference', which SCORING.md §0 requires at ship.
